Checked against checkout ea8b12a8a9894b5259c441eadd8f6f0c65e215af using targeted searches and incremental source reads. The checkout is unchanged. The supplied validation error is addressed by keeping this explanation below 10000 characters.

NOTATION
M=modular-tree, C=call-tree, O=ownership-tree, D=data-tree. Witness names below refer to nodes in those supplied trees. Diagram lines and jump columns are zero-based; span ends are exclusive. Each terminal tree line is a source-backed leaf. Branches express inclusion only. Singleton source anchors are treated as singleton slices.

CHECKED INTERSECTIONS
Each entry identifies concept, kernel K, and witnesses with their lens-specific roles. Degree equals the number of participating lenses listed.
1. Session construction; K=src/Surface.zig:477-477. M/S exposes init; C/Surface.init activates construction; O/Core Surface assigns session ownership.
2. Application dispatch; K=src/App.zig:164-164. M/A exposes tick; C/Main-thread message dispatch activates draining; O/CoreApp/bookkeeping assigns mailbox responsibility.
3. Owned derived policy; K=src/Surface.zig:144-144. M/C/consumer settings defines the no-borrowed-config boundary; O/Core Surface/config assigns ownership.
4. Conditional reload; K=src/Surface.zig:1804-1804. C/updateConfig activates replacement; O/main-thread config assigns replacement responsibility; D/T/C computes effective policy.
5. Safe teardown; K=src/Surface.zig:829-829. M/S/lifecycle defines the boundary; C/Session closure activates teardown; O/Core Surface/lifetime orders releases.
6. Binding-first input; K=src/Surface.zig:2792-2792. M/S/Keyboard defines event policy; C/keyCallback activates it; D/W/U needs bindings and retained sequence state to determine disposition.
7. Action dispatch; K=src/Surface.zig:4941-4941. M/S exposes performBindingAction; C/performBindingAction dispatches commands; D/H/navigation and D/W/payloads compute host requests or terminal input.
8. Shared font acquisition; K=src/font/SharedGridSet.zig:96-96. M/F exposes ref; O/CoreApp/font_grid_set assigns reference-counted ownership.
9. Font-grid switching; K=src/Surface.zig:2536-2536. C/Size-font activates switching; O/Font lease transfers old-key release; D/G/B computes metrics from settings and requested size.
10. Geometry propagation; K=src/Surface.zig:2618-2618. C/resize activates propagation; D/G computes dimensions from screen, padding and cells.
11. Terminal initialization; K=src/termio/Termio.zig:254-275. M/P exposes initialization; D/T/defaults needs policy and geometry.
12. Locked parsing; K=src/termio/Termio.zig:705-761. M/P defines the parsing boundary; O/io/terminal_stream assigns persistent parser ownership; D/T computes terminal state from bytes and prior state. C's literal processOutput anchor is 702, so it does not increase this kernel's degree.
13. VT dispatch; K=src/termio/stream_handler.zig:188-188. M/P/StreamHandler bridges protocol and session services; C/PTY output invokes dispatch; D/T needs decoded actions for edits and requests.
14. Screen storage; K=src/terminal/Screen.zig:45-87. M/T/storage defines state; O/io/terminal/Screen assigns ownership of pages, selection and protocol state.
15. Snapshot production; K=src/renderer/generic.zig:1371-1371. M/R exposes updateFrame; C/Rendering loop invokes it; D/F needs terminal-derived data for frames. Snapshot ownership has separate evidence, not a fourth witness to this kernel.
16. Paste admission; K=src/Surface.zig:6264-6264. C/Clipboard completion invokes admission; D/W/paste needs bytes, modes and protection policy.
17. Search fan-out; K=src/Surface.zig:1496-1496. C/Search loop invokes the callback; D/X/search derives highlights and UI counters.
18. Shared terminal access; K=src/renderer/State.zig:13-20. M/R defines the shared-state contract; O/renderer_state identifies its mutex and borrowed terminal pointer.
19. App resources; K=src/App.zig:137-148. M/A defines shared font/device services; O/CoreApp assigns their shutdown lifetime.
These retained intersections span all four input trees. None of these kernels has four literal witnesses. Data-participating intersections identify computational coupling; modular/ownership-only intersections describe implementation boundaries.

REJECTED CANDIDATES
Broad Surface support does not make key encoding and search destruction the same concept: that fails I2. Registration and runtime allocation are distinct responsibilities, not interchangeable ownership witnesses. The terminal mutex and draw_mutex protect different state despite broad renderer-range overlap. Font-metric demand and font-set allocation are related, but their cited slices do not directly meet; font switching supplies the joint instead. Semantic agreement alone cannot replace a common kernel.

STRUCTURE AND READING ORDER
Read session contracts/lifetime, then duplex IO/authoritative state, then derived geometry/frames/search. Each canvas progresses from entry/resource contracts through computation to consequences. Construction, reload and teardown bind canvas 1. Byte transport and mode-dependent encoding bind canvas 2. Shared fonts, snapshots and viewport invalidation bind canvas 3. Search follows frames because snapshot refresh supplies its viewport-dirty signal.
A canvas per lens would duplicate entities and require four canvases. A module-only hierarchy would conceal asynchronous hand-offs. A Surface-only call tree would obscure reusable terminal semantics and app-shared resources. The chosen hierarchy combines boundaries, lifetimes and computational needs. It is a selected core spine, not an exhaustive enumeration of gestures, protocols or inspector operations.

SOURCE CORRECTIONS
setCellSize does not call Surface.resize: it updates cells/padding and queues IO resize directly. Screen resize separately mails the renderer. Thread.renderCallback, not Renderer.updateFrame, calls drawFrame and arms the animation timer. Reload is not globally transactional: initial derivation failure retains the old Surface config, but later failures can occur after replacement. App.deinit deinitializes remaining registered runtime surfaces before releasing shared resources; deleteSurface itself neither destroys nor frees wrappers. POSIX output uses a gather thread plus a parsing reader. Read-only filtering gates Surface.queueIo writes, not protocol replies sent directly through Termio's mailbox. Terminal access and drawing use distinct mutexes. processOutput begins at 705. endUpdate is explicitly called outside the terminal lock; work is deferred into it, rather than its invocation being a Zig defer. Termio reconfiguration does not restart command/cwd.

RELATIONS AND DIMENSIONS
depends=modular dependency, calls=activation including marked asynchronous hand-offs, owns=lifetime responsibility, needs=data requirement. Jump spans carry their relation type. All endpoints are leaves in different diagrams. At the fully expanded frontier lifting is identity; coarser views lift endpoints, drop self-loops and merge parallel edges. Containment remains solely in the ASCII hierarchy.
Actual versus targets: 3 canvases / 3; diagrams per canvas 3,3,3 / 3-4; intra-canvas edges 6,6,6 / about 6; inter-canvas incidences 3,3,4 / about 3. Five jumps average 3.33 incidences: the extra incidence preserves separate geometry and snapshot dependencies. Total: 46 leaves and 23 cross-diagram relations. Maximum depth is 4 edges from graph root: root > canvas > diagram > cluster > leaf. No depth target was specified. Diagrams occupy rows 0,20,40 without overlap. Both later canvases are reachable from the first.
